It says nothing about production reachability or the mode flag being enabled in live traffic. This is consistent with the established convention used throughout THIS SAME FILE for sibling boxes: task 1.4 and 1.5 (both already `[x]`, unedited by this batch) close their checkboxes while their own Progress/Receipt notes explicitly state 'Mode stays off, so neither the guard nor the refusal is reachable in production' as a residual OUTSIDE the box's text, not a blocking condition on the checkbox. Task 1.6's own row is function-mechanism-shaped, not deployment-shaped; task 1.7 (still `[ ]`, untouched) is the box that explicitly owns 'reviewed cutover flag ... new matches admit through the journal' -- i.e., production-cutover reachability is a DIFFERENT box's text, not 1.6's. S6-R1 is explicitly an ordering constraint on task 1.7/S7 ('create-path seeding must land before any cutover flip'), not a defect in what 1.6's own two clauses claim. S6-R2 notes fragile-but-currently-passing mutant coverage (M4 IS killed, just by only one row), which is a maintenance note for future changes, not evidence the row's current claim is false today.
perEditTable.liveTestRun: npx jest --runTestsByPath src/lib/multiplayer/server/__tests__/matchCommitJournalHead.sqlite.test.ts --runInBand -> PASS, 7/7 tests, covering both clauses: 'the expected revision for a commit comes from the journal head' (3 rows, including the mode-enabled path) and 'the expected-head race' + 'duplicate-command refusal on the journal-head path' (4 rows). The row's literal text does not carry a 'live under enabled mode' clause, and requiring one here would be inconsistent with how the identical convention is applied to sibling rows 1.4/1.5 in the same file (which this batch did not touch and which are not in dispute). No required edit.
